transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
There are new details in the investigation of the mid-air attack aboard a commercial plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.
The United Arab Emirates, which is leading the probe, has deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack.
NPR's Kat Lonstorf reports from Tel Aviv.
Investigators in the UAE announced that the Fly Dubai co-pilot, who carried out the attack mid-flight,
assaulted the captain of the plane using what's called a crash axe,
a lightweight emergency tool stored in the cockpit to break through panels or jam doors in the event of a crash.
Investigators said the attacker then tried to seize control of the plane's flight mechanisms.
The plane had 174 people on board, many of whom are Israeli.
Israeli officials had already deemed it an attempted terrorist attack.
Emirati investigators have now agreed.
Both the pilot and co-pilot are live and being questioned, and the investigation is ongoing.
Israel has said the attacker is from Oman, although that has yet to be confirmed by Emirati, Saudi, or Omani officials.
Kat Lonstorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
President Trump is doubling down on his promise of $5,000 checks for Americans
if Republicans keep control of Congress after next month's midterms.
In a video posted on Truth Social this morning, Trump reiterated his pledge from the Oval Office.
If Republicans win the House of Representatives and the Senate,
I'm going to give all adult citizens in the United States of America $5,000.
And Republicans can do it, and Democrats can't,
because we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs and record-setting economic success.
But Democrat policies won't allow this to happen.
The proposed checks would require congressional approval, and some Republicans oppose the expense.
The pledge comes as Democrats seek an investigation into taxpayer-funded ads promoting Trump,
saying they violate federal law.
The White House defends those ads as public service announcements.
It was a mixed week on Wall Street as bond yields continued to climb.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports mortgage rates rose more than 7 percent.
Mortgage rates are closely tied to the yield on 10-year treasuries,
which jumped to their highest level in more than two decades this week.
Bondholders are demanding higher returns in response to stubborn inflation,
a ballooning federal debt, and competing demand for credit from big tech companies
that are shoveling lots of money into artificial intelligence.
On Friday, the Labor Department delivered a weaker-than-expected jobs report,
showing U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs last month.
Investors now think it's less likely the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates
when policymakers meet later this month.
For the week the Dow fell one-and-a-quarter percent,
the S&P 500 index slipped by a quarter percent,
and the NASDAQ rose a little less than half a percent.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR.
Ten people were injured after a man drove into a crowd in the Australian city of Newcastle today.
Scott Mayman reports the incident occurred as fans lined the streets
to show support for the city's rugby team.
The incident marred what was supposed to be a football grand final
for Australia's main rugby league competition.
Eyewitness Caitlin Lilly says fans had lined the streets
as the team was on a bus heading out of town on the eve of the grand final.
It's like a party atmosphere, I guess you could say,
and just in a split second, everything changed.
Assistant Police Commissioner Dave Waddell says it appears to have been a young driver
who was not acting responsibly behind the wheel.
Unfortunately, a young 18-year-old driving erratically has lost control of the vehicle
and gone into the crowd.
The driver was detained by several fans until police arrived who then arrested him.
For NPR News, I'm Scott Mayman in Canberra, Australia.
Basketball star Caitlin Clark's new signature sneakers sold out
in two hours on Nike's website.
Nike says the Caitlin Ones were launched in 5,000 retail stores,
the largest signature shoe launch in the company's history.
Clark's Indiana fever were eliminated from this year's WNBA playoffs
after losing to the Las Vegas Aces Thursday night in the first round.
The price of diesel continues to rise in the U.S.
AAA puts the national average at $6.35 per gallon.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: UAE deems mid-air attack on Fly Dubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv as attempted terrorist attack
Co-pilot assaulted captain with crash axe and attempted to seize control of aircraft with 174 people aboard
President Trump reiterates promise of $5,000 checks for Americans if Republicans win House and Senate
Bond yields climbed to highest level in two decades, mortgage rates rose above 7 percent
Labor Department reports U.S. employers added only 29,000 jobs last month, weaker than expected
Stock market mixed for week: Dow fell 1.25 percent, S&P 500 fell 0.25 percent, NASDAQ rose
Man drives vehicle into crowd at rugby event in Newcastle, Australia, injuring ten people
Eighteen-year-old driver detained and arrested after driving erratically into Newcastle crowd
Basketball star Caitlin Clark's signature Nike sneakers sold out in two hours
National average price of diesel reaches $6.35 per gallon, continues to rise
